subject: Request: provenance & architecture pack for SIG/CAIQ review - Clearwater Systems
messages:
From: Claire Wong <claire.wong@clearwater-sys.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: provenance & architecture pack for SIG/CAIQ review - Clearwater Systems

Hi Vivek / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Clearwater's SIG questionnaire cycle we need a compact provenance and architecture pack that shows how Redwood's Dedicated and Private deployment modes isolate customer data and control egress. The SIG lead asked for the following items by EOD Fri: 

- a single-page network diagram annotated with control boundaries (control plane vs data plane)
- a short provenance README describing what systems touch customer payloads and where logs are persisted
- a CSV control matrix mapping SIG/CAIQ controls to Redwood artifacts (policies, runbooks, diagrams)
- a short note on KMS/HSM boundaries and where keys are stored (cloud KMS vs customer KMS)

If you can provide draft artifacts (PDF/PNG/CSV) and a drive link, that will speed the SIG review. Please copy security@clearwater-sys.com.

Claire
Claire Wong
Security Program Manager, Clearwater Systems
claire.wong@clearwater-sys.com
+1 415-555-0218

Attachments: none

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 12:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: provenance & architecture pack for SIG/CAIQ review - Clearwater Systems

Claire — thanks for the clear ask. Kimberly and Marissa are looped for the technical diagram and control mapping respectively. Plan:

1) I will assemble a single compressed package (diagram PNG, control_matrix CSV, provenance_readme.md) and share a Drive link by Thu EOD Pacific.
2) Kimberly will verify the control plane / data plane annotations for Dedicated and Private (noted differences: customer VPC peering vs on-prem airgap).
3) Marissa will add the runtime touchpoints and the token-level logging locations for the README.

Quick clarifications before we finalize: do you prefer customer-managed KMS entries to be redacted in the public package (we can provide a redacted diagram plus a separate KMS appendix if needed)? Also confirm whether the SIG team wants the attachment filenames to include production timestamps.

We plan to include:
- network_diagram_v2.png (annotated: control-plane/data-plane, egress breakpoints, KMS boundary)
- control_matrix_q1.csv (SIG controls mapped to artifacts + links)
- provenance_readme.md (list of services that touch customer payloads and log destinations)

Attaching a short draft stub of the diagram and the control matrix as CSV stubs for early feedback.

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.png (stub), control_matrix_q1.csv (stub)

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Security (inbox)
Redwood Inference

Vivek / Marissa / Claire — quick technical note. I reviewed the initial stub and made two changes to the diagram:

- consolidated the control-plane endpoints into a single management layer (controlplane.redwood.internal) with strict peering ACLs to Dedicated pools (no inbound from customer networks)
- added an "egress inspection" hop for Private (on-prem) deployments that shows optional outbound proxying through customer-approved gateways (annotated)

The provenance README will include a table with service names, envs, and whether payloads are stored, cached (KV), or merely proxied. For KMS: we will represent customer-managed KMS endpoints as placeholders in the diagram (Customer KMS) and include a one-paragraph appendix describing redaction practices.

I uploaded an updated PNG (network_diagram_v2.png) and a short provenance_readme.md to the shared drive link below.

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.png (updated), provenance_readme.md

—Kimberly

Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek / Kimberly / Marissa — received and this looks great. The drive link and the CSV mapping are sufficient for the SIG intake. Two small asks before we mark the item closed: 

1) Could you add a one-line legal-friendly blurb in the README that we can paste into our SIG submission about Redwood's non-persistent handling of customer payloads in transit?
2) Please provide a signed attestation PDF for the control matrix (we can accept a scanned signature).

If those two items are added Monday I can move Clearwater's SIG ticket forward. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Claire
